A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SemDiD and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite checklist relocation, appendix renaming, and added analyses.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original Best-of-N evaluations, RLHF experiments, probability and semantic-diversity analyses, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds parameter sensitivity studies, comparator evaluations, large-model experiments, and computational-budget comparisons.

M1.justification: The scoring equations, greedy reference group, orthogonal guidance, inter-group repulsion, harmonic gain, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Added parameter-setting guidance does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage remains ARC-Challenge, BBH, GSM8K, Minerva Math, CoQA, PubMedQA, MMLU-Pro+, both WMT16 translation directions, and TLDR. The added sensitivity, scaling, and budget experiments reuse these tasks.

E2.justification: New Appendix I evaluates DoLa and 100-sample semantic clustering directly against SemDiD across the benchmark suite. Clustering existed in v1's selection analysis, but its inclusion in these head-to-head comparisons is new. The original benchmark comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds Qwen-2.5-70B evaluations and a stated equivalent-latency design using enlarged sampling pools and beam size 4. Appendices D.4–D.6 introduce controlled parameter sweeps. These are additional protocols; the original experimental settings and default-parameter table are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity analyses for lookahead depth, quality relaxation, harmonic strength, and transition timing, plus large-model scalability and computational-budget analyses. The original debiasing and component ablations, beam/group analyses, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the probability-position standard-deviation bands. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures for the performance comparisons.

E6.justification: Original plots and ablation scores are retained, while Tables 4–7 and 9–11 add substantial sensitivity and comparison results. For example, Table 10 newly reports 70B, N=25 GSM8K scores of 99.8% for SemDiD and 99.1% for temperature sampling. These are new model-setting results, not improvements over v1's 3B results.

T1.justification: The quality and diversity guarantees, harmonic-gain derivative argument, and computational-complexity theorem and derivation remain unchanged in Section 3.3 and Appendix C. No new formal result or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: 1.4–5.2% Best-of-N coverage improvements, 15% faster RLHF convergence, and up to 2.1% higher accuracy. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: New discussions interpret parameter robustness, optimal transition timing, DoLa and clustering limitations, and reduced relative overhead with larger models. Some interpretations overstate their tables: Appendix I.2 claims a 2.0-point BBH gain over the best baseline, although Table 10 reports 89.2% versus clustering's 88.1%.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete SemDiD repository URL where v1 only asserted anonymous repository availability. Appendix D.7 adds practical tuning guidance, including fitting position-decay parameters with scipy.curve_fit. Existing pseudocode, default settings, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds distinctions from semantically diverse uncertainty estimation and Soft Reasoning, and Appendix I cites DoLa. Introduction citations remove Self-Instruct and WizardLM while adding DIDS and two surveys. These are localized changes to positioning and references.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. v2 adds localized explanatory passages, acknowledgments, and corresponding-author markers; moves the checklist before the appendices; and renames the original Appendix I as J after inserting a new Appendix I.

P2.justification: Seven new tables substantially expand the presentation of parameter sensitivity, baseline comparisons, scaling, and computational budgets. The budget table groups results by sample count and includes compute and latency columns. All 15 figures are retained, with some repositioning; existing tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful code-access information and potentially valuable sensitivity, comparator, scaling, and budget evidence absent from v1. However, D.5 attributes relative quality–diversity control to lambda although unchanged Equation 12 uses it only as a common positive score multiplier. Table 11's purported equal-latency comparison also reports +18% versus +33% latency. These unresolved inconsistencies affect important new evidence, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
